skill.displayName: Leaf Curling & Margin Scorch Diagnosis | 植物卷叶/焦边识别（干旱/病害）

version.changelog:
Initial release of smyx-leaf-curling-scorch-diagnosis-analysis:

- Enables high-resolution plant leaf image analysis using AI to detect leaf curling direction and leaf-margin scorch distribution.
- Integrates optional soil moisture sensor data to help identify likely causes such as drought, disease, pesticide or fertilizer issues.
- Provides prioritized diagnosis and actionable care suggestions for farmers across open-field, greenhouse, and orchard scenarios.
- Supports inspection via agricultural cameras, UAVs, or mobile apps, and can be integrated into agricultural IoT platforms.
- Includes strict open-id management and process controls for secure and accurate user/report tracking.
- Offers automatic generation and cloud-based querying of historical diagnosis reports, with results shown as clear Markdown tables.

llm.summary: This plant diagnosis skill uses expected cloud analysis, but it also includes under-scoped identity, account, token, history, and unrelated health/face-analysis behavior that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is plant leaf curling and margin-scorch diagnosis, and the main config does set a plant-specific scene code. However, bundled analysis components still handle generic video analysis, healthAiResponse/faceAnalysisResponse fields, body-constitution-style outputs, generic add/edit/delete APIs, and an unrelated human face/health API reference, showing real purpose drift.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md discloses cloud history and open-id use, but it broadly auto-triggers on plant media, automatically saves uploaded attachments locally, requires an open-id before analysis, asks for username or phone number if absent, and instructs the agent to read api-key values from config files as open-id values.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No obfuscated installer or destructive install behavior was found. The requirements include yaml==6.0.3 rather than the normal PyYAML package name, and a dev config contains private-IP service URLs, but the default common config points at public production URLs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Remote upload is coherent for cloud visual diagnosis, but the implementation accepts local files or arbitrary HTTP(S) URLs, sends user identifiers and auth headers through a broad request wrapper, can silently create/login an external account, and includes payment/recharge messaging beyond a simple diagnostic flow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The shared library creates a local SQLite database under workspace data, mutates the sys_user schema at runtime, and stores user profile fields plus token/open_token values. This persistent credential/account handling is high-impact and not clearly scoped to plant diagnosis.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending plant images/videos or URLs, an open-id that may be a username or phone number, and related report data to the provider’s cloud service. Treat the skill as also handling account creation/login and local token storage, and avoid using shared config api-key values as user identifiers unless the publisher clarifies that behavior and its retention/security controls.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: cloud report history is partly disclosed and can fit the service, but the artifact-backed generic CRUD methods, unrelated video/health/face analysis docs, and report-management surface exceed the plant-only purpose.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: an identifier can be needed for cloud report tracking, but username/phone collection, api-key-as-open-id instructions, silent account creation/login, and local token persistence are not proportionate or clearly bounded.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: the code and nested reference materials contain confirmed generic video wording and health/face response handling that conflict with the plant diagnosis framing.
[SQP-1] expected: Partly accepted: triggering on relevant plant media is expected for this skill, but automatic local saving and cloud processing need clearer user-directed confirmation.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: the artifacts do not clearly disclose enough about media upload, arbitrary URL submission, identifier transmission, token handling, local persistence, or cloud history retrieval before those behaviors are used.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Accepted: cloud history listing is a documented feature, but keyword-triggered retrieval and using config api-key values as identity data create report-exposure and secret-handling concerns without clear confirmation or authorization boundaries.
[suspicious.install_untrusted_source] expected: Downgraded as a supporting signal only: the private IP appears in a dev configuration, while the production config uses public service URLs; this alone would not justify review.
